evidence: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29-34 adds InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions with a flat scope union and optional teamId; the constructor (line 58) now takes this looser type instead of the discriminated-union InsightsBookingServiceOptions it took before (base SHA). {scope:'team', userId, orgId} with no teamId therefore compiles. safeParse at lines 62-63 then fails quietly: options becomes null, and buildAuthorizationConditions (lines 126-127) returns 1=0, so the caller gets empty results with no error. No non-test caller needs the looser type (grep finds none), so going back to z.input/z.infer of the schema costs nothing and restores the compile-time check.

The logic claim is accurate. At insightsBooking.ts:157-162, when an org has no child teams, userIdsFromOrg is [] even though teamIds (line 154) already contains orgId. So the userId/isTeamBooking=false branch (lines 166-169) is dropped, and personal bookings of direct org members are left out. However, this PR did not introduce it: the same ternary is in the base SHA version of insightsBooking.ts, and it copies the legacy logic in packages/features/insights/server/trpc-router.ts:86-101 (and events.ts:685 returns early in the same case). The diff only converts the syntax to Prisma.sql. It is a real parity/behaviour question worth a follow-up, but it is outside the scope of this conversion PR.

insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:294-299 (team scope) and 330-343 (org scope) only assert toEqual on Prisma.sql objects. The only test that runs SQL against Postgres is getBaseConditions (lines 480-484), and it uses scope 'user', whose condition (service line 135) has no ANY(${array}) binding. So the ANY(${teamIds}) / ANY(${userIds}) array parameter binding added at service lines 164, 168 and 201 is never checked at runtime. The PR description itself says the tests were not run. Adding a $queryRaw run for team/org scope would be a cheap, useful improvement, but it is test coverage, not a defect.

The claim is accurate: at insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:445-466, userEventType and userBooking are created, and they are only deleted at lines 494-500, after the expect at line 487. A failed assertion would leave those rows behind. But every test in the file uses the same no-finally pattern (testData.cleanup() after assertions at lines 302, 345, 365, etc.), and the base SHA version had exactly the same cleanup at lines 602-608. Fixtures use unique timestamp/random suffixes, so leftover rows are unlikely to break other tests. This is a hygiene improvement for the whole file, not a problem this PR introduced.
